description:
ServerName::dns_name / ServerName::ip_address / MailboxName::parse all take &str. Rust idiom would expose this via FromStr:

  impl FromStr for ServerName<'static> { type Err = IdentityError; ... }
  impl FromStr for MailboxName<'static> { type Err = IdentityError; ... }

(or the equivalent on the non-'static type if PKIX-68mt.21's lifetime decision goes the other way).

Caller impact:

* parse::<ServerName>() works in TryFrom / TryInto patterns.
* Serde derive can use FromStr to deserialize from a single string (avoiding the open question on internal representation).
* clap / argh / structopt derive-from-string works out of the box.
* Test ergonomics: 'example.com'.parse().unwrap() vs ServerName::dns_name('example.com').unwrap() — minor but pervasive.

The DNS-vs-IP disambiguation is the catch: ServerName has two text constructors. FromStr would have to do its own DNS-vs-IP detection. Recommend: ServerName::FromStr tries IP first (the IP-or-DNS grammar is unambiguous: DNS hostnames cannot start with a digit-followed-by-dot in their leftmost label*; actually they can: '1example.com' is legal LDH. The disambiguation rule used by std::net::SocketAddr is 'try to parse as IP, fall back to DNS', which is what FromStr should do).

(*Per RFC 952 leading digit was forbidden; RFC 1123 §2.1 relaxed this. So '1.2.3.4' parses as IP but also could in principle be a DNS hostname of 4 numeric labels; the convention is to prefer IP. Worth documenting.)

For MailboxName, FromStr trivially defers to MailboxName::parse.

Severity P3: additive (non-breaking to add later), low-impact, but standard-Rust idiomatic. Worth filing as 1.0 polish.
title: No FromStr impl on ServerName / MailboxName despite parse-from-str being primary use case
